reason: The provided text fragment (Exodus 32:25-29) does not explicitly contain Yahweh's statement that he doesn't owe loyalty to the people or that he considers replacing them. The passage depicts the punishment of the Golden Calf rebellion—Moses commanding the Levites to execute judgment, resulting in approximately 3,000 deaths—and subsequently blessing those who consecrated themselves to the Lord. While this demonstrates divine judgment for covenant violation, the specific theological claim about Yahweh's lack of owed loyalty and consideration of replacement appears in Exodus 32:10 (prior to this fragment), where God says to Moses: 'I will make of thee a great nation.' The present fragment shows the enforcement of punishment but not the explicit declaration of the statement in question.
